groups.name: Qilin
groups.profile: Also known as Agenda. Golang/Rust RaaS first observed July 2022 and the most prolific leak site on Ransomware.live (2,559 claimed victims); double extortion, with the operator controlling encryption modes. Back to volume after a single posting in №70: ten postings, seven of them inside one hour (11:24–12:25 UTC on Ransomware.live), most with screenshots but no descriptions.
groups.countries: United States (3), Germany (3), Austria, Hungary, Japan, not disclosed (1)
groups.sectors: Professional Services, Healthcare, Retail & E-Commerce, Transportation, Manufacturing, Other

groups.name: Interlock
groups.profile: First observed September 2024; double extortion against healthcare, government, education and technology in North America and Europe (CISA joint advisory, July 2025). Known for fake browser-update / ClickFix lures.

groups.name: Barracuda
groups.profile: Leak site tracked by Ransomware.live since 2026-08-06 (16 victims, 9 countries, 5.9 TB claimed across 12 victims). Today's posting releases "unsold" data free for a month, which suggests it also tries to sell stolen data.

groups.name: Direwolf
groups.profile: Dire Wolf: human-operated group first documented May 2025; Golang locker with Curve25519/ChaCha20, run by a small core team rather than affiliates; 139 claimed victims in 37 countries, ransoms up to $500,000.

groups.name: Hyflock
groups.profile: New group tracked since 2026-10-13 (12 victims, 10 countries); Ransomware.live advises treating its claims with caution until independently verified. Its posts carry long company profiles.

groups.name: LeakNet
groups.profile: Not tracked by Ransomware.live (its group page returns 404). Today's post names no organisation, only a hashtag.

groups.name: LockBit 5.0
groups.profile: LockBit 5.0 ("ChuongDong") came back in September 2025 after the February 2024 law-enforcement takedown; cross-platform payloads for Windows, Linux and ESXi, affiliate model; 393 victims on Ransomware.live since December 2025, with an average 75-day lag from attack to claim.

groups.name: Shiba
groups.profile: Brand-new leak site: first victim discovered 2026-10-29, five so far (Germany, UK; healthcare, food, professional services). No published tactics profile.

groups.name: Whitearmor
groups.profile: New leak site tracked since 2026-10-23 (18 victims, mostly US technology and transport); Ransomware.live flags it as emerging and unverified.
